facts.claim: key: 0 is a key, while null, undefined, an empty string and an empty array are keyless. String keys split on dots and replace bracket segments matching [wordCharacters] with dot segments; array keys supply literal segments, so ["a.b"] differs from "a.b".

limits: This is not a general JavaScript property-expression parser; quoted bracket notation is not normalized by that bracket replacement.

facts.claim: When a control has multiple registered fields, Formly composes validators from participating fields whose internal hide state is false. It also collects validators through keyless child groups. Shared control validity therefore need not belong to only the widget being edited.
facts.context: shared control validators visible fields keyless groups validation ownership
limits: This describes Formly composition; it does not make independent validity or disabled-state guarantees for widgets sharing a control.

facts.claim: When a fields input change is processed with a form present, FormlyForm calls clearControl recursively, clearing synchronous/asynchronous validators and internal field registrations. The form extension can then install configured composed validators during the rebuild.

limits: Do not assume ad-hoc control.setValidators additions survive every fields rebuild. Existing manually supplied controls require integration-specific verification; internal registration helpers are not a recommended application API.

facts.claim: reverseDeepMerge fills destination properties that are null, undefined or an empty string by cloning source defaults. It preserves false and zero, and recursively merges objects only when both are objects with the same prototype and neither is an array.
facts.context: reverseDeepMerge defaultOptions null empty string false zero object prototype
limits: This configuration-merge rule differs from model defaultValue fallback, which is limited to eligible undefined model values.

facts.claim: reverseDeepMerge does not recursively merge arrays. An existing destination array, including an empty array, survives this default-filling operation; a null, undefined or empty-string destination instead receives a clone of the source value.
facts.context: reverseDeepMerge arrays empty wrappers defaultOptions concatenation
limits: This is the reverse-default merge, not every array operation in Formly and not a promise that all configuration merge utilities use this policy.
